newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Acma gets boost from Hayes merger.
newsitem.headline: Acma gets boost from Hayes merger.

text.p: Electronics-based Acma Ltd shares rose on Friday on news U.S. associate Hayes Microcomputer Products would be getting a back-door listing on Nasdaq by merging with Access Beyond Inc.
Acma shares hit a high of Singapore $2.55 in early morning trade before easing to S$2.48, up six cents at 0134 GMT. Volume was moderate at 130,000 units.
Access and Hayes said on Wednesday they had agreed to merge in a stock swap and Access will be renamed Hayes Communications and its stock will continue to trade on Nasdaq.
On completion of the merger, Access shareholders will own about 21 percent of the company while Hayes shareholders will own the remaining 79 percent.
Acma bought a 28 percent stake in Hayes in April last year when Hayes was valued at US$70 million.
The merger deal, however, valued the merged entity, Hayes Communications, at US$399 million.

Although Acma would have a smaller stake of 19 percent in Hayes after the merger, its shareholding is now worth about US$64.4 million based on Access's closing price of US$5.9375 on July 29, said an Acma statement.
Hayes is the world's number two modem maker and Access is a provider of remote access computer products.
